content: The optimal timing for delivery in women with an uncomplicated twin pregnancy at term remains uncertain. There is clinical support for both elective delivery at 37 weeks of gestation and expectant management, which involves waiting for spontaneous labor to begin naturally. The objective of this study was to evaluate the outcomes of a policy of elective delivery at 37 weeks compared to expectant management in women with otherwise uncomplicated twin pregnancies. The researchers conducted a systematic search of the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group's Trials Register as of December 12, 2013. They included randomized controlled trials that compared outcomes in mothers and infants who underwent elective delivery at 37 weeks with those managed expectantly. At least two independent reviewers assessed the eligibility and quality of the trials and extracted data for analysis. Two randomized controlled trials were included in the analysis, involving a total of 271 women and 542 infants. One trial was determined to have a low overall risk of bias, while the other trial had an unclear risk of selection bias, performance bias, and detection bias. The results showed no statistically significant differences between elective delivery at 37 weeks and expectant management in terms of cesarean section rates (risk ratio [RR] 1.05; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.83 to 1.32), perinatal death or serious perinatal morbidity (RR 0.34; 95% CI 0.01 to 8.35), or maternal death or serious maternal morbidity (RR 0.29; 95% CI 0.06 to 1.38). Additionally, no significant differences were observed in secondary maternal and infant outcomes, including hemorrhage requiring blood transfusion, instrumental vaginal birth, meconium-stained amniotic fluid, Apgar scores below seven at five minutes, neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admissions, birthweight below 2500 grams, neonatal encephalopathy, or respiratory distress syndrome. However, one study found that elective delivery at 37 weeks significantly reduced the risk of infants being born with a birthweight below the third centile (RR 0.30; 95% CI 0.13 to 0.68), although this was not a pre-specified outcome of the review. The authors concluded that elective delivery at 37 weeks of gestation in women with an uncomplicated twin pregnancy does not appear to increase the risk of adverse outcomes for mothers or infants. These findings align with the recommendations of the United Kingdom's National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE), which advises delivery at 37 weeks for women with dichorionic twin pregnancies. The authors also noted that it is unlikely there is sufficient clinical equipoise to justify randomizing women to delivery at a later gestational age.
